Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Vitalis MedTech Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, CEO; Emily Carter, CFO; Dr. Michael Reyes, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Wong, Chief Commercial Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Vitalis MedTech demonstrated significant progress this quarter, driven by our focus on innovation, operational excellence, and strategic partnerships.

Today, I will cover seven key aspects of our performance: revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter and year; organic revenue growth by segment and geography; competitive dynamics and market share trends; strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter; FDA approvals and CE marks obtained; key assumptions underlying the guidance; and inventory management and working capital optimization.

Emily will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. Dr. Reyes will offer insights into our technology roadmap, and Lisa will discuss our commercial strategies. Afterwards, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with revenue and margin guidance for the next quarter and year.

In the third quarter, we delivered revenue of $1.28 billion, up 11% as reported and 12% organically, powered by robust procedural volumes in our Structural Heart franchise, especially our next-generation TAVR valve, the VitalFlow Ultra, which gained an additional 250 basis points of U.S. market share against leaders like Edwards Lifesciences' Sapien and Medtronic's Evolut. Gross margin improved 120 basis points to 68.5%, thanks to efficiencies at our new Galway, Ireland facility and a favorable mix from high-margin disposables.

Turning to Q4 2024 guidance, we anticipate revenue between $1.36 billion and $1.39 billion, implying 10% to 12% reported growth or 11% to 13% organically. This accounts for ongoing strength in procedure-driven segments, tempered by typical Q4 seasonality in elective orthopedics and about a 1-point foreign exchange headwind from a stronger U.S. dollar versus the euro and yen.

By segment: Cardiovascular & Structural Heart, which is 58% of revenue, should see mid-teens organic growth, fueled by U.S. TAVR penetration surpassing 25% in high-volume centers and initial international launches of VitalFlow Ultra in key CE Mark regions. Our drug-eluting stent line, VitalStent Sirolimus, posted 18% U.S. growth in Q3 as PCI volumes rebounded post-flu season. Orthopedics & Spine, at 22% of revenue, expects low double-digit growth from our robotic-assisted knee system, Apex Robotics Platform, now live in 350 U.S. sites and challenging Stryker's Mako and Zimmer Biomet's ROSA, plus expansion into Japan through our Terumo partnership. Neuromodulation & Diagnostics, 15% of revenue, should be flat to low single-digits as we compare against tough prior-year DBS rechargeables launches, offset by 22% growth in our AI-powered EEG diagnostics. Other categories, like endoscopy consumables, see modest gains.

For margins, gross margin is guided to 68.5% to 69.0%, lifted by volume in high-margin Structural Heart disposables, declining resin costs after inflation peaks, and $45 million in annualized savings from our LEAN+ manufacturing program year-to-date. Operating margin targets 25.0% to 25.5%, balancing investments like adding 150 sales reps in Emerging Markets and R&D at 12% of revenue. Adjusted diluted EPS comes in at $1.72 to $1.76, suggesting 9% to 12% growth on about 425 million shares outstanding.

For full-year 2025, we're raising confidence above our long-term 8-10% growth target, guiding revenue to $5.85 billion to $5.95 billion, or 11% to 13% reported and 12% to 14% organically—a notch above prior views. Tailwinds include U.S. medtech procedure growth of 5-7% per Symphony Health data, accelerating into 2025 with pent-up demand in electrophysiology and structural interventions, where our 120+ basis points market share gains position us to outperform. Product launches like VitalFlow Prime TAVR with AI-optimized deployment—FDA submission in Q1 2025—next-gen leadless pacemaker with pivotal data in H1, and Apex Robotics spine extensions will add 300-400 basis points to growth, akin to Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci 5 impact.

Regionally: U.S., 65% of revenue, eyes 13-15% organic growth with CMS NTAP reimbursement for TAVR and Value-Based Care deals with 20+ IDNs boosting premium disposables attach to 15%. Europe, 20%, targets 8-10% despite EU MDR challenges, as our Galway site achieves full compliance, unlike some rivals. Asia-Pacific and Emerging Markets, 15%, aim for 18-20%, with China tenders giving VitalStent 15% volume share and orthopedics ramps in Brazil and India amid demographics.

FY2025 gross margin: 69.0% to 69.5%, via supply chain dual-sourcing for stents and valves, 2-3% ASP hikes on premiums, and robotics scale. Operating margin: 26.0% to 26.5%, R&D at 11.5-12%, adjusted EPS $7.45 to $7.65—up 11-15% midpoint—with 20-22% tax and $200 million repurchases. Free cash flow at $1.4 billion, or 24% margin, backs 15%+ dividend hikes and buybacks. We're advancing our Precision MedTech vision with AI/ML in diagnostics and robotics, $150 million for electrophysiology tuck-ins to grow our 25% EP position. Risks include U.S. reimbursement shifts, FX—$100 million revenue per 5% EUR move—and competition like J&J's Abiomed integration, countered by diversified lines and $500 million inventory.

Now, let's talk about organic revenue growth by segment and geography.

On an organic basis, excluding our NeuroStim Solutions acquisition and FX headwinds, total revenue grew 9.2% for the full year to date, speeding to 11.5% in Q4 of last year, driven by procedure volumes, share gains, and pipeline ramps. This highlights our edge in high-growth medtech amid demographics, minimally invasive shifts, and value-based reimbursement.

Cardiovascular, 42% of revenue, led with 12.8% organic growth full year, 15.2% in Q4, from structural heart like VitalValve TAVR surging 18% with 22% U.S. procedure jumps versus Edwards and Medtronic, and electrophysiology up 11% via VitalMap 3.0 AI mapping boosting ablation success 15% in PROSPECT-EP. TAVR penetration under 20% globally leaves room; $250 million R&D targets percutaneous mitral valve for 2026, a $5 billion market. ASP dipped 1-2% on acuity mix, but volumes dominated.

Orthopaedics & Spine, 28% of revenue, hit 7.5% organic full year, 9.1% Q4, with hip/knee recon up 8% on Trinity cementless stem gaining 3 points to 12% U.S. share over Stryker's Triathlon. Spine flat at 6% from U.S. budgets, but FlexiCore expandables up 14% in ASCs; ORTHO-VALUE registry shows 20% faster recovery. VitalRobotics Spine limited release sets up 15%+ 2024 growth against Intuitive and Zimmer in $2 billion market.

Advanced Surgical Technologies, 18% of revenue, grew 10.3% organic full year, 13.4% Q4, with endoscopy +12% on PureScope single-use scope to 25% U.S. penetration post-infection recalls like Pentax/Olympus. Robotics +22%, VitalBot Xi at 1,200 installs, service/instruments +35%; ASP +2% on haptics. Hybrid OR with GE Healthcare eyes 20% CAGR to 2028.

Diabetes & Patient Monitoring, 12% of revenue, up 6.9% organic full year, 7.8% Q4, CGM +11% via VitalSense patch with Apple HealthKit adding 500,000 users over Dexcom G7; insulin softer at 4% from GLP-1s, countered by closed-loop upgrade improving time-in-range 12% in CLARITY-2. myVitalMed app at 2 million MAUs drives 25% adherence, subscription potential.

Geographically balanced, U.S.-heavy: Americas, 62%, 11.2% organic full year, 13.9% Q4; U.S. 12.1% on 8% volumes per Vizient, Canada/LATAM from GPOS/Brazil normalization. EMEA, 22%, 6.8% full year, 8.5% Q4; NHS/DRG offset by France/Italy tenders, MDR resolved. APAC, 13%, 8.4% full year, 10.2% Q4; China +15% on TAVR/CGM reimbursement, Japan robotics, India ASCs; Singapore manufacturing vs. tariffs. Rest of World, 3%, 5.1%, Middle East +12%.

Outpacing medtech index by 400 bps, +1.5 share points per Evaluate; 18 launches, 75% quota attainment, $1.2 billion M&A. Risks: rare earths, PBMs; FY24 organic 10-12%, cardio/surgical mid-teens in $600 billion market.

Moving on to competitive dynamics and market share trends.

In the $52 billion structural heart and interventional cardiology market growing 9.2% CAGR to 2028—fueled by aging, aortic stenosis, transcatheter shifts—we expanded global TAVR share 150 bps YoY to 17.8% in Q3 per internal/Millennium data, sixth straight quarter, full-year +220 bps. Coronary stents steady at 14.2% global, +110 bps; DES to 16.5% vs. Boston Synergy/Abbott Xience, Prominence sirolimus stent 22% new U.S. wins per ProcedureWatch.

Structural heart battle with Edwards/Medtronic at 65% TAVR share (Sapien/Evolut); Edwards Sapien 3 Ultra +12%, but ApexFlow's SkirtGuard cut PVL to <2% in ORBIT-3 vs. 5-7% average, 1,200 U.S. sites, 28% low-risk share. Medtronic Evolut FX stroke risks ~2.5% vs. our 1.4% ESC-noted. LAAO: Watchman FLX 52% U.S., our Sentinel-X +4 to 18%, 15% faster procedures in SWISS. Abbott Amulet EU pressure, but PEEK imaging next-gen rebounds.

Trends: hybrid imaging +35% YoY, fits Philips Azurion/Siemens Artis. Bioresorbables traction; Prominence RESORB 95% strength at 12 months, 12% EU share pre-IDE. Supply resilience: 99.2% delivery vs. Terumo's shortages.

Regions: U.S. 48% revenue, 52% structural share at 21.4%, CMS TAVR 2.0; Europe 28% sales, + to 15.2% CE renewals, Germany DRG +€45M; APAC +18% YoY, China to 8.5% NMPA Prominence, target 12% FY25 vs. MicroPort pricing; EM 6% +22% percutaneous.

$285M R&D +14%: AI ApexAI -22% contrast, valve-in-valve for 10-15% redos, GE robotic LAAO for $2B TAM 10% by 2027. $450M VascuTech buy +300 bps DES. Fortress balance sheet amid J&J Abiomed; #3 player #1 growth, +100-150 bps FY24.

Next, strategic priorities and focus areas for the next quarter.

Q3 revenue hit $1.35 billion, +14% YoY, EBITDA margin +220 bps to 28.5% from structural heart leverage/efficiencies. Q4 guide: 10-12% growth, $1.45-1.48B, organic 9-11% high-end, assuming 105% U.S. elective recovery, nitinol/PEEK inflation. Margins 28-29%.

Pillars: innovation acceleration, commercial execution, operational resilience.

Innovation: VitalFlex Robotic Navigation full U.S. ramp post-510(k), 15 cath labs incl. Mayo/Cleveland; Q4 50+ deploys, $75-85M revenue, +150% seq., 22% robotic peripheral share over Intuitive Ion haptics/precision. CardioAI Suite +18% efficiency, -25% fluoro in IDEAS, Q4 PMA submit vs. Abbott Navifinder/BSX Polaris. R&D 12.5%, $45M BurstDR+ SCS closed-loop +35% relief vs. Medtronic Intellis, Q3 implants.

Commercial: U.S. structural heart $320M Q3 +28%, Q4 intermediate-risk +3 pts to 15% ProcedureIQ, CMS pass-through $4,200 vs. Sapien. APAC 22% Q3 to 25% YE, China NMPA VitalFlex tenders Shanghai/Beijing 10-15% $2.5B robotics. Europe OrthoFusion AR knee 20 centers post-CE vs. Stryker Mako; EMEA +16%. LATAM/India neuromod attach 12-18%. NTAs glucose biosensors $150M diabetes. Reps +14% procedures to 2.8 via training.

Resilience: titanium +8%, dual-source Vietnam/Mexico <15% risk, DIO 142, 98% delivery. ESG Scope 3 -12% bio-resins EU MDR. 150 AI/reg engineers, 20% female leaders. $800M M&A digital therapeutics like NeuroPace.

Q4 execution: VitalFlex scale, structural wins, foundation fortify for 12-14% FY organic in $550B medtech 5.2% CAGR.

Then, FDA approvals and CE marks obtained.

Transformative quarter: FDA PMA for CardioFlex DRX bioresorbable DES for high-risk PCI, IDE 1,200 patients/45 sites, 4.2% 12-month TLF vs. 7.8% predicate, 24-month resorption, Q1 Breakthrough expedited 30%/6 months. NeuroPulse DBS 510(k) AI adaptive for Parkinson's, -40% battery, +28% motor vs. Percept PC, 15% faster, $1.2B DBS <20% pen.

Europe MDR CE for CardioFlex/NeuroPulse by TUV SUD, 800 datasets/12 months vs. 18-24 avg., LivaNova delays. EchoVision AI IVUS CE, ML plaque char, -25% variability ESC.

U.S. covers 85% $4.2B pipeline TAM +20 pts YoY, $280M FY24 incr., 12-15% DES share 18 mos., 120 reps/J&J Cordis. EU €150M +35%, Milan hub tariffs. 18% R&D $320M adaptive trials/digital twins FDA AI plan. Value-based $12k savings CABG CMS bundles > Abbott Xience/Intuitive hybrid.

Q4 De Novo EchoVision, TAVR IDE vs. Sapien Ultra; tailwinds +22% gross reaffirm $2.8-3.0B rev 25-27% EBITDA.

Then, key assumptions underlying the guidance.

FY2024 guide $4.85-4.95B rev 7-10% organic, EPS $5.75-5.95, structural/peripheral momentum offset ortho reimbursement.

Assumptions: procedures 4-6% global +6-8% H2; structural heart 35% rev TAVR 8-10% Evolut PRO+ +2 pts PVL<1% PROPEL; peripheral DCB/atherectomy 5-7% diabetes PAD +12% CDC, no Japan Stellarex yet; ortho -1-3% Medicare, OrthoBot 25% attach Stryker-like.

Pricing flat-+0.5% US, -1-2% EU IVDR, +50 bps mix LAAC Watchman to 15%. Ops: gross 68-69% +100 bps Galway nitinol +150 bps resin -15%, 2% supply vs. 4% freight, Mexico China tariffs, capex 5% $200M automation 98% delivery.

Regions: US 55% 7-9% CMS 2.1% MPFS TAVR 6%; EMEA 25% 4-6% Germany -1.5% UK NHS $50M MDR $30M; APAC 15% 12-15% China 20% Suzhou Lotus, Japan 3% India 18%; Rest 5%.

R&D $650M 13.5% five H2 Phase III AI OCT Philips bioresorbables Absorb learnings; $300M peripheral like Penumbra +50 bps; digital remote 30% adopt 8% recurring.

Macro: USD/EUR 1.08 JPY145 CNY7.2, 50 bps EPS/5c EUR, infl 2.5% OpEx +6%, no rec 75th PVI LEK, FDA breakthrough no holds.

Risks: site-neutral 1-2%, China delays 500 bps APAC, FX; upside robotics Intuitive, M&A. Disciplined in $550B TAM 2028.

Finally, inventory management and working capital optimization.

DIO 112 days Q-end -18% YoY from 137, best pre-COVID > Stryker 128/BSX 135; turns 3.2x +0.5x, $1.2B base. CCC 78 days -22, unlocked $245M FCF funds 65% R&D no debt.

AI demand sensing SAP/Palantir 92% acc +14%, HL7 surgeon vol/CMS/backlogs; high-vel EndoGrip safety -25% to 34 days no stockouts. VMI top10 40% consignment $180M off-sheet DPO 72 +12%; SKU -15% 220 legacy $95M obsolete.

Regions: US 55% DIO95 Memphis JIT CHIPS; Europe 25% 135 MDR NeuroStim Germany sterilization -20% LT; APAC 15% 105 China/India dual Taiwan; LATAM 5% +30% consignment.

Electives +12% Definitive, GPO Vizient; H2 -10 DIO blockchain IBM traceability 100% lots FCF $900M FY24 $2.5B M&A robotics Intuitive-adj. ROIC 18.2% top peers, titanium +15%/resins +22%.

I will now turn the call over to Emily for a review of our financial results.

Emily Carter:
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan highlighted, we achieved strong financial results this quarter, with revenue of $1.28 billion up 12% organically, gross margins at 68.5%, and robust free cash flow supporting our capital allocation. Expenses were well-controlled, with OpEx at 43.5% of revenue reflecting R&D investments and commercial expansion, leading to adjusted operating margins of 25.1%. Profitability metrics exceeded expectations, and our balance sheet remains fortress-like with $2.1 billion in cash and low leverage. For Q4 and FY2025, as detailed earlier, we see continued margin expansion and EPS growth, underpinned by the assumptions shared. Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Reyes for an update on our product pipeline.

Dr. Michael Reyes:
Thank you, Emily. We continue to invest in cutting-edge technologies. Our development of VitalFlow Prime TAVR is progressing well, and we anticipate it will revolutionize structural heart interventions with self-expanding design and AI-optimized deployment. R&D efforts are focused on bioresorbable scaffolds like CardioFlex DRX, robotic platforms such as Apex and VitalFlex with haptic precision, AI tools like CardioAI and EchoVision for plaque and lesion assessment, neuromodulation advances in NeuroPulse DBS and BurstDR+ SCS closed-loop, and imaging integrations for hybrid ORs. We've hit key milestones like IDE trials, pivotal data readouts, and submissions, with $650 million committed this year to fuel Phase IIIs, partnerships with Philips and GE, and digital twins for faster regulatory paths. Our pipeline positions us to outpace market growth in TAVR, robotics-adjacent spine, EP, and diabetes monitoring, targeting multiple $1-5 billion TAMs.

Next, Lisa with some insights on our commercial strategy.

Lisa Wong:
Thank you, Dr. Reyes. Our commercial team has been instrumental in driving adoption of our products. We are focused on expanding our market presence and enhancing customer engagement through rep expansion—adding 150 in EM—targeted tenders in China and Japan, IDN partnerships for VBC attach rates up to 15-18%, site-of-care shifts to ASCs, GPO wins with Vizient/Premier, and training via VitalCore University. U.S. structural heart and robotics ramps, Europe MDR-compliant launches, APAC localization like Suzhou JV, and EM distributor realignments are key. Reimbursement pursuits like CMS NTAP extensions and NTAs unlock upside, while hybrid OR bundles and KOL advocacy at ESC drive procedural excellence and share gains.

Now, back to Johnathan for Q&A.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Lisa. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star one. Our first question comes from Mike Lawson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Lawson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the Q4 guidance, how much of the organic growth is baked from VitalFlow Ultra international ramps, and any update on FX sensitivities?

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, Mike. VitalFlow Ultra CE Mark launches contribute modestly to Q4 at 1-2 points of organic, scaling into 2025 with Japan/Terumo tailwinds. FX is a 1-point headwind Q4, sensitivity $100 million revenue per 5% EUR move as noted—our hedges cover 70% through H1 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Great, thanks. Regarding inventory optimization, what gives you confidence in further DIO cuts H2 amid titanium inflation?

Emily Carter:
Sarah, our AI Palantir forecasting at 92% accuracy, VMI 40% with top suppliers, and blockchain pilots enable the 10-day H2 reduction. Dual-sourcing Mexico/Vietnam caps titanium exposure despite +15%, with 98% delivery already. ROIC at 18.2% reflects this resilience.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
Thanks. On commercial, how are you penetrating intermediate-risk TAVR, and APAC robotics outlook?

Lisa Wong:
David, intermediate-risk sees 3-point share gain to 15% Q4 via CMS $4,200 pass-through outperforming Sapien economics, plus ORBIT-3 PVL data with KOLs. APAC robotics: China NMPA fast-track tenders mid-Q4 for 10-15% $2.5B market by 2025, Suzhou localization offsets tariffs.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim:
Thanks. CTO, on the AI pipeline like ApexAI and CardioAI, timelines for broader adoption and competitive edge?

Dr. Michael Reyes:
Laura, ApexAI beta reduced contrast 22% at 50 sites, integrates Philips/Siemens for hybrid procedures +35% trend; expanded PMA Q4. CardioAI 18% efficiency/25% less fluoro IDEAS data challenges Navifinder/Polaris—year-end approval. Adoption via 120-rep training, targeting 20% premium attach in EP/PCI.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your insightful questions. We are dedicated to driving innovation and delivering value to our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
